## Verdict
REVISE — Sender-visible completion, retry-loss identity, and interval-aware ceiling semantics need explicit contracts before the comparisons are trustworthy.

## Critical gaps
- Define sender-visible transport outcomes. Legacy `_stage` gates DATA on `_send`’s remote-reception result. Timed donor decisions, retry scheduling, and action unlocks must depend only on local transmission completion, timeouts, or paid received replies—not hidden receiver loss or commit results.

## Important improvements
- Define frame/reassembly identities and retransmission behavior. Existing `_lost` gives every same-contact retry identical segment losses; introduce stable per-attempt samples without coupling them to heap execution order.
- Specify ceiling eligibility using contact overlap with publication, expiry, and observation windows. Retaining the old oracle’s whole-round expiry guard would undercount valid timed deliveries. Keep the legacy oracle path unchanged.

## Validation gaps
- Counterfactual receiver loss/commit-failure tests: donor-visible behavior remains identical until an explicit reply or timeout.
- Same-contact retries receive distinct loss samples; replay, ordering, and cancellation preserve samples for unchanged attempts.
- Mid-contact publication/expiry and post-horizon publications: ceiling dominance and identical offered-delivery denominators.

## Recommended revision
1. Freeze transport observability, transaction/reassembly, timeout, and loss-identity contracts; add the targeted tests.
2. Implement shared timed mechanics, then round-gated and live modes, preserving legacy behavior.
3. Add the interval-aware observer ceiling; run the proposed regression suite and complete matched comparison matrix.

## Acceptance Contract
Acceptance level: attested
